columns: BARMM LABOUR MARKET & SIPP ALIGNMENT — DECISION DASHBOARD

rows.BARMM LABOUR MARKET & SIPP ALIGNMENT — D: Phase II policy analysis | 2025 labour market baseline | 2026 SIPP investment-priority framework

rows.column_7:
KEY DECISION SIGNAL
High employment coexists with rising underemployment. The SIPP provides the investment-priority lens, but project maturity and employer evidence must determine actual workforce demand. Prioritise value-chain productivity, industry-linked skills, local supplier capacity and decent work.

rows.BARMM LABOUR MARKET & SIPP ALIGNMENT — D: Notes: LFS indicators are official PSA estimates. GRDP shares (2024) and employment shares (2025) have different reference years and denominators; comparison is descriptive, not a productivity ratio. SIPP activity counts reflect mapped activity groups, not project counts, investments or jobs.

rows.column_2: Supporting dataset and source register for the revised Phase II policy paper.
All figures are drawn from the cited official/statistical sources or MTIT–BOI project documents.
Investment leads are not approved investment or confirmed employment demand. GRDP and employment shares refer to different years and are not a productivity ratio.
Use the Data Dictionary sheet for definitions and the Source Register for citations and URLs.
Do not add personal or confidential employer-level information without Client authorisation and appropriate safeguards.
The SIPP Workforce Map lists 45 mapped activity groups from the approved 2026 SIPP. Indicative occupations and competencies are analytical inferences, not confirmed BARMM vacancies or shortages.
